name: Keratosis Pilaris Atrophicans

criteria.description: Presence of follicular hyperkeratotic papules primarily on the face and scalp
Progressive scarring alopecia in affected areas
Atrophic and cicatricial skin changes in areas of follicular involvement
Positive family history of keratosis pilaris atrophicans or related disorders
Histopathological confirmation showing follicular plugging and perifollicular fibrosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (follicular hyperkeratosis, scarring alopecia, and atrophic skin changes) with supportive histopathology or family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing may be considered in atypical cases.

laboratory: Histopathology showing follicular plugging, perifollicular fibrosis, and lymphocytic infiltrate
genetic: Mutations in genes related to keratinization (e.g., possible involvement of KRT genes) reported in some familial cases
other: Clinical examination reveals characteristic follicular papules with scarring alopecia

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of atrophic skin changes and scarring alopecia
More prominent inflammation and bacterial infection

redFlags: Secondary bacterial infection with systemic symptoms
Extensive atrophic skin changes leading to functional impairment
